spec.description: Where the budget stands today and where it is heading. There is no month selector here on purpose: an envelope balance is a running total, so "what was in the fund last March" is a curiosity, while "what is in it now and will it cover the next bill" is the question. For how a closed month went against budget, use the budget strip on Monthly Review. Accounts are not a filter either - a budget belongs to a category, whichever card paid.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT sum(budget) AS "Budgeted"
FROM v_budget_status WHERE (array_length(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR category = ANY(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[]))

spec.description: The current month's accrued budget for the selected categories.
spec.title: Budgeted

spec.rawSql:
WITH m AS (
    SELECT (month::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'America/Denver') AS t,
           to_char(month, 'YYYY-MM') AS label,
           category, budget, spent, variance
    FROM v_budget_vs_actual
    WHERE NOT carry_forward
)
SELECT label AS "Month", category AS "Category",
       budget AS "Budget", spent AS "Spent", variance AS "Over/under"
FROM m
WHERE $__timeFilter(t) AND (array_length(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR category = ANY(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[]))
ORDER BY variance ASC
LIMIT 12

spec.description: The monthly categories that went furthest over, worst first. Envelope categories are left out because a single month over accrual is normal for them - the Envelopes table is where they are judged.
spec.title: Worst Months

spec.rawSql:
WITH m AS (
    SELECT (month::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'America/Denver') AS t,
           category, envelope_balance
    FROM v_budget_vs_actual
    WHERE carry_forward
)
SELECT t AS "time", category AS metric, envelope_balance AS value
FROM m
WHERE $__timeFilter(t) AND (array_length(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR category = ANY(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[]))
ORDER BY 1, 2

spec.description: Each envelope's balance month by month: climbing while it accrues, dropping when the bill lands. Below zero is underfunded. The months past today assume no further spending, so the forward slope is the best case - a bill due next month is not subtracted until it is actually charged.
spec.title: Envelopes Over Time

spec.rawSql:
SELECT c.name AS "Category",
       to_char(p.valid_from, 'YYYY-MM') AS "From",
       p.amount AS "Per period",
       p.period AS "Period",
       round(p.amount / budget_period_months(p.period), 2) AS "Monthly",
       CASE WHEN p.carry_forward THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS "Rolls over",
       p.opening_balance AS "Opening balance",
       coalesce(p.note, '') AS "Note"
FROM budget_plans p
JOIN categories c ON c.id = p.category_id
WHERE (array_length(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR c.name = ANY(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[]))
ORDER BY c.name, p.valid_from DESC

spec.description: Every row you have ever loaded, newest first per category - the audit trail for what you changed and when. A blank Per period is a deliberate stop: budgeting for that category ends from that month. Opening balance seeds an envelope, or re-baselines it to the real fund balance.
spec.title: Budget Plan History

spec.rawSql:
SELECT sum(spent) AS "Spent"
FROM v_budget_status WHERE (array_length(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR category = ANY(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[]))

spec.description: Spending so far this month in those categories and their descendants.
spec.title: Spent

spec.rawSql:
WITH s AS (
    SELECT coalesce(sum(spent), 0) AS spent, sum(budget) AS budget
    FROM v_budget_status WHERE (array_length(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR category = ANY(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[]))
)
SELECT round(100.0 * (spent / (extract(day FROM current_date) / extract(day FROM date_trunc('month', current_date) + interval '1 month - 1 day')))
             / nullif(budget, 0), 1) AS "Pace"
FROM s

spec.description: Spending so far, stretched over the whole month, as a share of budget. 100% means you are exactly on track to spend the budget; 130% means you are heading 30% over if the rest of the month looks like the start of it. Jumpy in the first few days, by design - it is a projection.
spec.title: Pace

spec.rawSql:
SELECT sum(envelope_balance) AS "In envelopes"
FROM v_budget_status WHERE carry_forward AND (array_length(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR category = ANY(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[]))

spec.description: Total set aside across every carry-forward category - the money that should be sitting there waiting for periodic bills.
spec.title: Envelope Total

spec.rawSql:
SELECT CASE WHEN count(*) = 0 THEN NULL
            ELSE count(*) FILTER (WHERE envelope_shortfall > 0) END
           AS "Underfunded"
FROM v_budget_status WHERE carry_forward AND (array_length(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR category = ANY(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[]))

spec.description: Envelopes that ran dry this month: the accrued money was spent past, and the shortfall was forgiven rather than carried as a deficit. The most actionable number on this dashboard - it is the month an envelope failed to cover what it was for. A balance can no longer go negative, so this, not a minus sign, is the warning.
spec.title: Underfunded

spec.rawSql:
SELECT category AS metric, pct_used AS value
FROM v_budget_status
WHERE NOT carry_forward AND (array_length(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR category = ANY(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[]))
ORDER BY pct_used DESC NULLS LAST

spec.description: Monthly categories only - the ones judged on the month alone. Amber past 80% of budget, red past 100%. The bar is capped at 150% so one blown category does not flatten the rest; the number beside it is the real figure.
spec.title: Budget Used

spec.rawSql:
SELECT s.category          AS "Category",
       s.period            AS "Period",
       m.plan_amount       AS "Per period",
       s.budget            AS "Monthly",
       s.spent             AS "Spent this month",
       s.envelope_balance  AS "Balance",
       s.months_of_cover   AS "Months covered"
FROM v_budget_status s
JOIN v_budget_months m ON m.category_id = s.category_id
                      AND m.month = s.month
WHERE s.carry_forward AND (array_length(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR s.category = ANY(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[]))
ORDER BY s.envelope_balance ASC NULLS FIRST

spec.description: Carry-forward categories, worst first. Per period is the bill itself; Monthly is what it accrues at. Balance is the fund as of this month, and Months covered is how many months of accrual that balance represents - under 1 on a bill due soon is the thing to act on. A negative balance means you are behind.
spec.title: Envelopes

spec.rawSql:
WITH days AS (
    SELECT generate_series(date_trunc('month', current_date)::date,
                           (date_trunc('month', current_date)::date + interval '1 month - 1 day')::date,
                           interval '1 day')::date AS d
), plan AS (
    SELECT coalesce(sum(budget), 0) AS budget
    FROM v_budget_status WHERE (array_length(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR category = ANY(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[]))
), daily AS (
    SELECT v.posted_on AS d, sum(v.outflow) AS amt
    FROM v_spending v
    WHERE date_trunc('month', v.posted_on)::date = date_trunc('month', current_date)::date
      AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM v_budget_status s
                   WHERE s.category_id = ANY(v.category_id_path)
                     AND (array_length(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR s.category = ANY(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[])))
    GROUP BY 1
), run AS (
    SELECT days.d,
           sum(coalesce(daily.amt, 0)) OVER (ORDER BY days.d) AS cumulative,
           plan.budget
    FROM days
    CROSS JOIN plan
    LEFT JOIN daily ON daily.d = days.d
)
SELECT (d::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'America/Denver') AS "time",
       CASE WHEN d <= current_date THEN cumulative END AS "Spent so far",
       round(budget * extract(day FROM d) / extract(day FROM date_trunc('month', current_date) + interval '1 month - 1 day'), 2) AS "Budget pace"
FROM run
ORDER BY 1

spec.description: Spending this month adding up day by day, against a straight line to the month's total budget. Above the line means you are ahead of pace. The spending series stops at today rather than running flat to the month end. An EXISTS test picks the budgeted transactions so a transaction cannot be counted twice when a category and its parent both have plans.
spec.title: Month's Pace

spec.rawSql:
WITH m AS (
    SELECT (month::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'America/Denver') AS t,
           category, spent, budget
    FROM v_budget_vs_actual
)
SELECT t AS "time", sum(spent) AS "Spent", sum(budget) AS "Budget"
FROM m
WHERE $__timeFilter(t) AND (array_length(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[], 1) IS NULL OR category = ANY(ARRAY[${category:sqlstring}]::text[]))
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

spec.description: Bars are what you spent, the line is what the plans accrued, summed over the selected categories. Months past today are budget with no spending yet - that is the plan reaching forward, not a collapse.
spec.title: Budget Versus Spending
